ab_the_white_imperialist.blurb: This sport crag sits partway down the canyon at Grassi Lakes, above the Bow Valley outside Canmore. It is a single-pitch wall with a bigger overhang toward one side and blockier ground on the other. Of its 19 routes, about half are 5.10, with a few 5.12s and a scattering of easier lines from 5.7 to 5.9, so it suits climbers working through the middle grades. The wall faces east and gets sun for much of the day. Grassi Lakes as a whole is known for steep, pocketed limestone, and this wall offers a more vertical alternative.

ab_cartel_boulder.blurb: Cartel Boulder is a small sector in the House Area on the northwest side of Frank Slide, in Alberta's Crowsnest Pass. It holds 16 bouldering problems with an unusually wide spread: a few easy lines around V0 and V1, a couple of V3s, and a cluster of much harder problems from V6 up to V10. The enormous House Boulder next door is generally too tall for bouldering. The trail in passes several other blocks first, and some boulders here are fairly sheltered from wind, which helps on days when the Chinook is blowing through the pass.

ab_kiss_the_sky_wall.blurb: Kiss the Sky Wall is a steep, sunny sport wall in Jasper National Park, in the Watchtower Creek drainage off the Maligne Valley. The 16 routes are aimed at strong climbers: most are 5.12, about five are 5.13, and a few 5.10 and 5.11 lines give a way to warm up. Expect single-pitch climbing with fixed anchors for lowering or rappelling. The wall faces roughly south-southeast and stays sunny into the late afternoon. Some lines drag the rope and a few spots stay damp, so plan how you will pull your ropes.
ab_kiss_the_sky_wall.approach: Walk the Watchtower Creek trail through forest until it reaches a narrow bridge made of lumber planks. Cross it and the wall is right there.

ab_raven_s_nest_buttress.blurb: Raven's Nest Buttress is the tallest and most talked-about wall at Carrot Creek, a sport area in the Bow Valley inside Banff National Park, reached by a long, mostly flat walk up the creek drainage. All 17 routes are bolted, mostly around 5.12, with a handful of 5.10s and 5.11s and a couple of 5.13s. The wall is steep and sustained, with smooth, water-worn slopers that give a pump unlike elsewhere in the valley. The creek is loud at the base, so agree on belay commands before leaving the ground.
